<XYChart> plots numeric x/y pairs as points, lines, or both. A third value can drive point size, and another can drive point colour. If you have used Grafana's XY Chart panel, every option there has a counterpart here; see Coming from Grafana.

Where the series come from

  • With <Series> children, each child is one series.
  • Without children, the series come from a Frame: the first field is x and every other field is a y series. A Vec<T> has no field names, so a chart with no children and a Vec<T> shows "No data".

The chart remembers which series you hid in the legend and which point is hovered. Give each chart a key when you render several of them in a loop, so that state stays with the right one.

Return f64::NAN from x or y to leave a row out.

Write the row type on the first closure of each tag. The other closures on that tag pick it up:

<Series x={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} y={|r| r.load} />

<XYChart> and <Series> both take these props. A value on the series wins over the chart's value, and the chart's value wins over the default.

Point size grows by area: a value twice as large gets a point with twice the area, not twice the diameter. The smallest and largest size values across all series map to the two ends of size_range.

The axis range starts at the data's extent, rounded out to tidy tick values (whole powers for a log scale).

  • soft_min / soft_max widen the range when the data doesn't reach them, but never narrow it.
  • centered_zero makes the range symmetric around 0.
  • min / max pin the range exactly, and data outside it is cut off.

A log scale ignores zero and negative values. With no data the range is 0 to 1.

The label, when you don't set one, is the field name if every series shares it, or the words common to the start and end of the field names. Only Frame data has field names.

Tick and tooltip text uses format if you set it. Otherwise it uses decimals. Otherwise the decimals are chosen from the tick spacing. format takes a closure that doesn't capture anything; end it with .into():

AxisConfig::new().format(|v| format!("{v:.0} °C").into())

Clicking a legend item shows only that series; click it again to show them all. Ctrl-click (Cmd-click on macOS) shows or hides a single series. Hidden series stay in the legend, dimmed. The axes rescale to the series still shown, while colours and point sizes stay the same.

Calcs

Calcs summarise each series' y values, skipping NaN. They always appear in this order, whatever order you list them in:

CalcShown asMeaning
First / LastFirst / Lastfirst / last value
Min / MaxMin / Maxsmallest / largest
MeanMeanaverage
MedianMedianmiddle value
SumTotalsum

RangeRangeMax - Min
DiffDifferenceLast - First
Variance / StdDevVariance / StdDevspread of the values

Tooltip

MethodArgumentDefault
Tooltip::single() / hidden()–single
max_widthPixelsnone
max_heightPixelsnone

The same Tooltip type is shared with <Trend>, which also uses Tooltip::multi(), sort and hide_zeros. The XY Chart shows multi() like single(), as Grafana's XY Chart does.

Hovering a point highlights it and shows a tooltip next to it. The tooltip has:

  • the series name and the point's colour;
  • the x and y values, each labelled with its field name or axis label;
  • the size and colour values, when the series has them.

Series with hide_from.tooltip are still highlighted on hover, but show no tooltip. Points from series drawn only as lines can't be hovered.

Color<T>Meaning
Color::fixed(color), or any Hsla / Rgbaone colour for the whole series
Color::by(value, scheme)each point is coloured by its value, through scheme
SchemeMeaning
GreenYellowRed, RedYellowGreen, BlueYellowRed, YellowRed, BluePurple, YellowBlue, Blues, Reds, Greens, Purples, Orangesgradients from the theme
Named("…")a gradient you added to your theme file
Scheme::gradient(colors)your own gradient
Scheme::thresholds([(value, color), …])fixed steps: a value takes the colour of the highest threshold at or below it, and values below the first threshold take the first colour

gradient and thresholds take a Vec or a &'static slice. Prefer a static slice: it costs nothing to rebuild on every render. See Static colour lists.

A gradient spans the smallest to the largest colour value across all series that colour by value, so equal values look the same in every series. Points with a NaN colour value use the theme's fallback colour.

MethodMeaning

Without <Series>, the size and colour fields aren't drawn as series of their own. Words shared by every series name are trimmed: cpu load host-a and cpu load host-b become host-a and host-b, and the y axis is labelled cpu load.

With <Series>, read fields by position (x={|r: &[f64; 3]| r[1]}) or by name (x={frame.get("Requests")}).

Your own data source

Implement Dataset<T> to chart data stored some other way:

pub trait Dataset<T>: 'static {
    // the rows (and the schema, for named fields), lent for the time of `f`
    fn read<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&[T], Option<Schema<'_, T>>) -> R) -> R;
    #[track_caller]
    fn revision(&self) -> Option<Revision> { None }
    // provided: `rows(|rows| ..)` and `schema(|schema| ..)`, both through `read`
}

pub struct Schema<'a, T> {
    pub names: &'a [SharedString],
    pub read: fn(&T, usize) -> f64,
    pub size: Option<usize>,
    pub color: Option<(usize, &'a Scheme)>,
}
MethodImplement it to
readcall f with the rows and, when the data names its fields, a schema. A signal's value lives in blenderui's signal store, so the rows are lent for the call rather than returned; don't read the same dataset again inside f.
revisionreturn a value that changes whenever the rows change. While it stays the same, the chart reuses its work; None derives again on every render. Charts call it while rendering. Revision::of(signal) builds one from a blenderui signal: a memo at the caller notices every write to it.
schema (in read)describe named numeric fields, so charts can build series (XY Chart) or bars (Bar Gauge) without accessors. read(row, field) returns one value; size and color pick fields for the XY Chart's auto mapping.

Vec<T>, Signal<Vec<T>>, Frame<N> and Signal<Frame<N>> implement it. A plain Vec or Frame has no revision, so keep chart data in a use_signal.

examples.title: Basic scatter
examples.description: One series of points with every default.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn basic_scatter() {
    let data = use_signal(readings());
    rsx! {
        <XYChart data={data} class="h-72">
            <Series name="Load" x={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} y={|r| r.load} />
        </XYChart>
    }
}

examples.title: Lines and points
examples.description: Show modes and line styles, set on the chart and overridden per series.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn lines_and_points() {
    let data = use_signal(curve(|x| x.sqrt() * 10., 0..=49));
    rsx! {
        <XYChart data={data} show={Show::PointsAndLines} point_size={4.} line_width={1.5} class="h-72">
            <Series name="√x" x={|p: &(f64, f64)| p.0} y={|p| p.1} />
            <Series name="√x · 0.5" x={|p: &(f64, f64)| p.0} y={|p| p.1 * 0.5} line_style={LineStyle::DASH} />
            <Series name="√x · 0.25" x={|p: &(f64, f64)| p.0} y={|p| p.1 * 0.25} show={Show::Lines} line_style={LineStyle::DOT} />
        </XYChart>
    }
}

examples.title: Colour by value
examples.description: A gradient scheme and a threshold scheme.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn color_by_value() {
    let data = use_signal(readings());
    rsx! {
        <XYChart data={data} class="h-72">
            <Series name="Gradient" x={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} y={|r| r.load}
                    color={Color::by(|r: &Reading| r.memory, Scheme::BlueYellowRed)} />
            <Series name="Thresholds" x={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} y={|r| r.load + 100.}
                    color={Color::by(|r: &Reading| r.load, Scheme::thresholds(&THRESHOLDS[..]))}
                    point_shape={PointShape::Square} />
        </XYChart>
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: A signal as data: the chart redraws when it is written.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live_signal() {
    let data = use_signal(readings());
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-72">
            <div class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline" onClick={move || data.update(|rows| rows.iter_mut().for_each(|r| r.load = (r.load * 1.7) % 90.))}>
                "Shuffle"
            </div>
            <XYChart data={data} class="flex-1">
                <Series name="Load" x={|r: &Reading| r.temperature} y={|r| r.load} />
            </XYChart>
        </div>
    }
}

examples.title: Log scale
examples.description: Log axis with soft and hard limits.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn log_scale() {
    let data = use_signal(curve(|day| 1.5f64.powf((day / 2.).floor()), 1..=40));
    rsx! {
        <XYChart
            data={data}
            show={Show::PointsAndLines}
            x_axis={AxisConfig::new().label("Day").soft_min(0.).soft_max(45.)}
            y_axis={AxisConfig::new().label("Requests").scale(ScaleKind::Log { base: 10. }).min(1.)}
            class="h-72"
        >
            <Series name="Growth" x={|p: &(f64, f64)| p.0} y={|p| p.1} />
        </XYChart>
    }
}

examples.title: Symlog on the right
examples.description: Negative and positive magnitudes on one axis.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn symlog_right_axis() {
    let data = use_signal(curve(|x| x.powi(3), -30..=30));
    rsx! {
        <XYChart
            data={data}
            y_axis={AxisConfig::new()
                .scale(ScaleKind::Symlog { base: 10., linear_threshold: 10. })
                .placement(AxisPlacement::Right)
                .centered_zero(true)
                .color_mode(AxisColorMode::Series)
                .border(true)}
            legend={Legend::hidden()}
            class="h-72"
        >
            <Series name="x³" x={|p: &(f64, f64)| p.0} y={|p| p.1} color={rgb(0x8839ef)} />
        </XYChart>
    }
}

examples.description: Calcs, sorting and right placement. Click to isolate, Ctrl-click to toggle.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn table_legend() {
    let data = use_signal(readings());
    rsx! {
        <XYChart
            data={data}

                .right()
                .width(px(220.))

}

examples.title: Series from a loop
examples.description: One series per column, generated in view!.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn series_from_a_loop() {
    let rows = use_signal(host_rows());
    rsx! {
        <XYChart data={rows} show={Show::Lines} class="h-72">
            {for (column, host) in HOSTS.into_iter().enumerate() {
                <Series key={column} name={host} x={|r: &Row| r.time} y={move |r: &Row| r.values[column]} />
            }}
        </XYChart>
    }
}
